Funding Announcement 
An announcement was made 08/01/2019 by 
Minister Ring on the results of the Outdoor 
Recreation Infrastructure Scheme. Offaly 
County Council were successful in getting 
funding for the following two extensions to the 
Grand Canal Greenway - Ballycommon 
Bridge to Campbells Bridge and Kilbeggan 
Branch of Greenway for €200,000 and 
Pollagh to Lough Boora Discovery Park for 
€200,000 
 
Launch of Midlands Regional Enterprise 
Plans to 2020  
The Midland Regional Enterprise Plan to 
2020 was launched by Minister Humphreys 
on February 6th 2019 in Mountmellick County 
Laois. The Plan seeks to increase the 
potential of the Midland Region to grow 
business, resilience, and create new 
employment opportunities, whilst bringing the 
unemployment levels to within 1% of the state 
average, ensuring that a greater number of 
people both work and live in the Midlands; 
and to see an improvement in labour force 
participation towards the national average. 
 
The delivery of the Plan will be overseen by a 
Steering 
Committee 
comprising 
of 
representatives from Local Authorities, state 
agencies 
and 
private 
business. 
The 
committee is chaired by Dr Anne Cusack, 
Critical Healthcare and Project Management 
is provided by Sarah Morgan.

Strategic Infrastructure Development 
Following discussion at the January Council 
meeting, the Chief Executive’s Report on the 
West Offaly Peat SID application was 
submitted to An Bord Pleanala.  
The application was for the continued use of 
the peat-fuelled power station to facilitate the 
phased transition to exclusive firing with 
Bio-Mass and associated development works 
at the existing West Offaly Power Station 
and existing ash disposal site at Derrylahan, 
Co Offaly.

Water Quality 
The collaboration which underpins the 
implementation of the Water Framework 
Directive as set out in the River Basin 
Management Plan for Ireland 2018-2021 was 
demonstrated in a recent conference on 
Farming Mitigation Options which was 
delivered to 
a capacity 
audience in 
Tullamore on 17th January which included 
staff from Local Authority, LAWPro, 
Agricultural Advisors and various interested 
parties.  
The 
conference 
demonstrated 
approaches 
to 
assessing 
the 
inter-
relationships between the farming activity 
and the natural water environment and how 
to implement practical and effective changes 
that will support the farming activity and the 
local water quality.  
The assessment of the Gageborough River is 
due to commence shortly and the Water 
Quality team have provided support to the 
LAWPro Catchment Assessment Team in 
this regard.  The Gageborough River is the 
source of drinking water for the Clara 
Regional Water Supply.  A community 
meeting takes place on Tuesday 12th 
February next in Horseleap/Streamstown 
Community 
Centre, 
Streamstown 
Co. 
Westmeath N91X81C from 7:30pm.  This 
meeting will inform the community about the 
planned work programmes involved and 
gather any local information that may help 
inform the process.

LOCAL ENTERPRISE OFFICE 
Ireland's Best Young Entrepreneur 
Competition 2019 
The Local Enterprise Office Offaly launched 
the Offaly stage of the Ireland’s Best Young 
Entrepreneur programme for 2019. LEO 
Offaly is looking for dynamic, innovative 
young business people from across Offaly 
county to enter the Ireland’s Best Young 
Entrepreneur 
2019 
competition. 
The 
competition invites 18-35 year olds who 
have a business idea, a start-up or an already 
established business to enter. Applying is 
quick and simple. It takes about 15 minutes, 
is free of charge and is done on 
www.IBYE.ie 
 
 
Brexit Seminar 
Members of the Local Enterprise Office 
Offaly attended the Brexit Seminar held on 
Friday 25th January in the Hodson Bay 
Hotel. The event was held to help staff in the 
Local Enterprise Offices around Ireland to 
actively engage with businesses to help in 
identifying and understanding the potential 
implications of Brexit and how the 
challenges can be addressed. 
The event discussed key challenges which 
Offaly business will be exposed to in the 
event of a hard Brexit. The main issues raised 
at the seminar were Brexit tariffs, supply 
chain issues, customs clearance delays, 
currency volatility, financial supports and 
technical advice available to business.

LIBRARY SERVICES 
The Polar Express 
The Polar Express interactive storytime was 
hosted in all 8 libraries with 9 performances.  
Over 450 children took part in this initiative.  
Family members also attended.  All venues 
were fully booked within one hour of the 
release of the tickets.  The event was also 
recorded by Midlands 103.  The reaction 
from the general public was very positive. 
Tullamore Library also hosted “A night 
before Christmas” event with the local 
creative group reading Christmas poetry and 
two local choirs singing Christmas Carols- 
the Offaly County Council Choir and Le 
Cheile.  This event was well attended. 
 
January 2019 
Lego model exhibition 
On Saturday 26th January, Brick.ie, the Irish 
Association 
for 
Adult Fans 
of LEGO®, 
put 
on 
a 
show of their amazing creations.  The 
opening hours of the building were extended 
to accommodate the event.  Most of the 
models on display have been designed and 
built by Brick.ie members and some of these 
have already received recognition of the 
highest order at international exhibitions.  A 
family play area with thousands of bricks 
was a feature on the day so everyone could 
join in the fun.  Over 1420 people attended 
the event in Birr Library.   
  
There are also Lego play therapy workshops 
held in Tullamore Library during January 
which were also fully booked. The Stem 
Saturdays in Tullamore are fully booked and 
there are weekly updates on the activities of 
the class on the Offaly Libraries Facebook 
page.

Harry Potter Night 
There will be two Harry Potter Night in 
Offaly this February.  On 
Thursday 7th February in 
Tullamore Library starting at 
3.30pm with wizard chess and 
in Edenderry on Wednesday 13th February 
starting at 6pm.  These events are fully 
booked.  Raven Haven will be in both 
locations with their beautiful birds.  There 
are fun events for all Harry Potter fans both 
young and old. 
 
March 2019 
Daingean Library is trialing new opening 
hours to increase accessibility to the library 
service in the town.  From the 2nd March, 
Daingean library will be opening at the 
following times: 
- 
Wednesday:   1.30 – 5.00pm & 6-
8pm 
- 
Saturday: 
10am – 1pm 
There is now wifi access in the building and 
5 public access computers with fibre 
broadband.
